trigger: AMEND-01's C6c control failed on its first evaluation: the observed 10x2 random-design kappa -0.44000000000000006 lies at rank 7 of 2000 in its own Monte Carlo null (0.35th percentile), outside the central 95% interval [p2.5=-0.37931, p97.5=0.32894].
diagnosis: C6c was itself mis-calibrated, not the estimator. A single-draw central-95% interval check is a hypothesis test with a 5% false-failure rate by construction; it is not a calibration test. The observed draw is a legitimate extreme draw of the same generator (rank 7/2000, null mean -0.053965, null sd 0.1918). The substantive implementation test is C6b (200x2 independent design -> kappa -0.0303, |kappa| < 0.20), which passed; C6a (identical -> 1.0) passed.

amended_control.C6c_kappa_null_calibration: REPLACED single-draw percentile-tail test by a pre-declared 3-sigma plausibility rule: |k_obs - mean(null)| <= 3 * sd(null), with the observed rank and percentile reported alongside. Rationale: sd(null) at the original 10x2 design is 0.1918, so the 3-sigma band is ~[-0.63, 0.52]; a correct estimator's draw has ~0.3% false-failure probability against this rule, versus 5% for the superseded rule. The 200x2 design (C6b) remains the primary valid test because its SE is ~0.05.
